note: Research output 2026-10-05. Every slug and url was checked by literal match in lib/library-data.ts, lib/cinema-data.ts, lib/resources-data.ts. Titles, pitches and prompts are DRAFTS for Mary Kate to edit. Re-verify before use, the catalogs change.

topics.title: Who gets to play disabled characters?
topics.pitch: From My Left Foot to Echo, the long fight over whether nondisabled actors should ever play disabled roles, and who gets hired behind the camera.
topics.prompt: Should a nondisabled actor ever play a disabled character, and what would it take for casting to actually change?

resources.name: GADIM: Global Alliance for Disability in Media and Entertainment
Disability Belongs: Entertainment and News Media

topics.note: Deepest topic in the catalogs (25 items). The catalog text itself names the debate: my-left-foot is described as the most-cited example of cripping up (lib/cinema-data.ts, my-left-foot entry), and the-war-on-wheels-podcast covers authentic casting and cripping up. a-different-man is the live counterexample (nondisabled lead in prosthetics, disabled co-star). Both https://www.respectability.org and https://disabilitybelongs.org/entertainment/ exist as separate resources (RespectAbility was renamed Disability Belongs), so pick one to avoid showing the same org twice. The library entry respectability-hollywood-disability still uses the old name.

topics.note: The catalogs include both sides (Ladd and Lane for the cultural model, Chorost's Rebuilt as a cochlear implant memoir, That Deaf Kid arguing for balance), which matters for a fair 'What do you think?' box. Editorial caution: the prompt is worded to ask about conflicts and missing voices rather than inviting hearing people to rule on Deaf children. Deaf U is catalogued as controversial inside the Deaf community.

gaps: AI audio description and synthetic voices: zero catalog items on it (searched AI, synthetic, text-to-speech, TTS, generative, avatar). Only adjacent hooks exist (against-technoableism-shew; human narrator material like ADNA and reid-my-mind-radio). Add the American Council of the Blind guidelines on text to speech in audio description, https://www.acb.org/node/9229 (I fetched it: it says human-voiced AD remains the gold standard and allows TTS only under conditions such as blind-professional review and audience transparency). A search snippet also cites ACB Resolution 2021-22 favoring human voices; I did not verify that on a primary page.

Website accessibility overlays: zero catalog items (the only overlay matches are unrelated, like the WAVE visual overlay). Add the Overlay Fact Sheet, https://overlayfactsheet.com/en/ (fetched: a critique of overlays endorsed by over 1,048 professionals) and the FTC action against accessiBe, https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/04/ftc-approves-final-order-requiring-accessibe-pay-1-million (found in a search restricted to ftc.gov; I did not open the page itself, so confirm before citing). Existing digital resources such as axe (catalogued as catching about 30 percent of issues) would support it but do not address overlays.

Caption glasses and personal caption devices: no catalog item mentions them. Add the NAD page on caption access in movie theaters, https://www.nad.org/resources/technology/caption-access-in-movie-theaters/ (fetched: covers Sony Entertainment Access Glasses and CaptiView and says NAD still advocates for open captioning). This would complete the open-captions topic.

Access doulas: the word doula appears in none of the three catalogs. Access riders have only one entry (Access Docs for Artists). Needs new items before it can stand alone; it is currently folded into access-labor.

Person-first versus identity-first language and video game accessibility: no dedicated items found (language: no matches for identity-first, person-first or terminology guides; games: one fiction title and a mention in the FilmDis description, nothing in cinema). Not worth publishing yet.

Disabled comedians (not in the 14 above, extra option): strong in video and books but with zero resources. Cinema: josh-blue-sticky-change, ryan-niemiller-unarmed-and-dangerous, lost-voice-guy-cerebral-lolsy, hannah-gadsby-douglas, drew-lynch-concussed, pushers-rosie-jones, jerk-bbc, what-the-deaf. Library: find-another-dream-zayid, mean-little-deaf-queer, too-late-to-die-young. Good for a lighter, video-heavy topic if one resource or two is added.

Assisted dying and the right to die (optional, sensitive): only three entries (unspeakable-conversations, life-after-davenport-2025, and the NYT essay resource at https://www.nytimes.com/2003/02/16/magazine/unspeakable-conversations.html). Thin, and it needs Mary Kate's editorial call and moderation thought before a public What do you think box.
Cinema column is empty for relaxed-performances and nearly empty for alt-text (only adjacent spoken description items), so those two need at least one video item each to match the rest of the page.

The Instagram reels idea has no support in the data: no catalog entry links to Instagram, so reels would have to be added as new items with their own field (for example an outbound link card rather than an embed).
